name: Nolan Reed
life: “I still remember taking down a shop sign too early after an argument.” On Sunday, near Ferris Deli, Nolan asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I brought the shopkeeper a new sign and discovered she wants the old one saved as evidence of what happened.
appearance: Nolan is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread, Nolan looks down for a moment before saying something difficult when listening.
personality: Nolan prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To save the old sign as part of the record.
family: Val Moss is Nolan’s half-sibling. Nolan brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Val makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The engine lullaby*, Val says, “I can't hear it from our new flat. I walk here after arguments so I don't say the cruel thing first.”
connections: Sofia Cruz. The new sign cannot settle the case until the words heard on the original call are distinguished.

reactions.situation: A newspaper repeats the old display caption
reactions.response: Nolan gets the shopkeeper's preferred wording to the editor before passing the story on.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Nolan gives up their own space if possible and asks the passengers who arrived first to choose what happens next.
